newsitem.title: MEXICO: Synkro sets 3.960 bln peso capital boost.
newsitem.headline: Synkro sets 3.960 bln peso capital boost.

text.p: Mexican textile firm Synkro said on Monday it had approved a capital increase of 3.960 billion pesos at an extraordinary shareholders meeting held July 31.
Synkro said in a statement it would issue new shares to increase its fixed capital by 500 million pesos and the variable part of its capital by 3.460 billion pesos.

Shareholders will have the pre-emptive right to subscribe to one new share for each existing one held on August 20 against a cash payment of 0.036 pesos. The pre-emptive right expires August 21, Synkro said.
The company said it would also undertake a reverse stock split.

"The reverse split will consist of the issuance of one new share in substitution of every 100 shares that conform the capital stocks after the capital increases approved ... have taken place and will become effective no later than August 21, 1997," the statement said.
The company added that the shareholders had also approved the conversion of each series B into a series A share on a one-to-one basis once capitalization had been completed.
Any shares not subscribed to by current shareholders will be offered to Synkro's financial creditors and shareholders who made a cash contribution to future capital increases, the company said.
